mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of lines are intersecting lines?

options.A: Two lines that are parallel and never meet.
options.B: Two lines that cross each other at a single point.
options.C: Two lines that lie on top of each other (coincident).
options.D: Two lines that are skew, existing in different planes.

mcqs.answer: Two lines that cross each other at a single point.
mcqs.explanation: Intersecting lines are defined as lines that meet at exactly one point. Option B describes this situation. Parallel lines never meet, coincident lines are the same line, and skew lines are non‑coplanar and do not intersect.

mcqs.question: Line l passes through points (2,3) and (5,7). Line m passes through points (2,3) and (8,3). What is the point where the two lines intersect?
mcqs.explanation: Both lines share the common point (2,3); therefore this is the point of intersection. The other points belong to only one of the lines, and the lines indeed intersect, so option D is false.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise perpendicular lines as intersecting lines forming right angles
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between perpendicular lines?

options.A: Perpendicular lines intersect and form a right angle.
options.D: Perpendicular lines intersect at any acute angle.

mcqs.answer: Perpendicular lines intersect and form a right angle.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, perpendicular lines meet at a point and the angle between them is exactly 90°, a right angle. Options B, C, and D contradict this definition.

mcqs.question: In a diagram, line AB is drawn horizontally and line CD is drawn vertically, intersecting at point O. Which relationship is shown between AB and CD?

options.C: Intersecting lines that are not perpendicular

mcqs.explanation: A horizontal line and a vertical line meet at a right angle, which is the definition of perpendicular lines. They are not parallel, they do intersect, and skew lines are non‑coplanar, which does not apply here.

mcqs.learning_point: Use geometric reasoning to compare line relationships
mcqs.question: Consider three pairs of lines: (i) two lines that cross at 45°, (ii) two lines that are parallel, (iii) two lines that cross at 90°. Which pair best illustrates intersecting lines that are not perpendicular?
mcqs.explanation: Intersecting lines are those that meet; pair (i) meets at 45°, which is intersecting but not perpendicular. Pair (ii) is parallel (no intersection) and pair (iii) is perpendicular, so they do not satisfy the condition.

mcqs.question: On a city map, Oak Street runs east‑west and Pine Street runs northeast‑southwest, meeting at a single junction. How should their relationship be described?
mcqs.explanation: The two streets meet at one point, which makes them intersecting lines. They are not parallel because they do meet, they are not perpendicular because the angle is not 90°, and skew lines are a three‑dimensional concept not applicable to a flat map.

mcqs.question: A student claims that any two lines that meet at a point must be perpendicular. Which statement corrects this misconception?

options.A: Only perpendicular lines meet at a point; other lines never do.
options.B: Intersecting lines can meet at any angle, not just 90°.
options.C: Parallel lines also meet at a point.
options.D: Skew lines are the same as intersecting lines.

mcqs.answer: Intersecting lines can meet at any angle, not just 90°.
mcqs.explanation: Intersecting lines simply share a common point; the angle between them can be acute, obtuse, or right. Only when the angle is exactly 90° are they called perpendicular. Options A, C, and D are false statements.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise perpendicular lines as intersecting lines forming right angles
mcqs.question: If two lines intersect and form a right angle, which of the following statements must be true?
mcqs.explanation: A right angle (90°) between two intersecting lines is the defining property of perpendicular lines. Therefore statement B is always true. Parallel lines never intersect, coincident lines are the same line, and skew lines do not intersect in a plane.
